To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of the expert finding system is significantly affected by the choice of the social network.

(1) the use of social network data for the task of expert finding can be improved if one considers the social network topology and not only the user profiles, (2) the use of the social network topology for the task of user profile completion can be improved if the user profiles and the topology information are used jointly, and (3) the use of user profile completion techniques for expert finding is not always beneficial.
the performance of the proposed methods is significantly better than that of the baseline methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to find the right crowd for a given expert finding problem, i.e., how to find the best set of experts for a given problem.
the problem of expert selection in the context of social networks.
the problem of finding experts in a social network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of the right crowd is an essential part of any expert finding process.
there are a number of different ways to find experts, and that there is no single best way.
social media marketing is a powerful tool for businesses, but it is also a tool with a lot of potential to be misused.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is important to select experts based on their social connections, but not based on their social influence.
, given an arbitrary set of experts, we propose a new approach to find a set of experts that is representative of the entire set of experts.
we propose a new method to find experts in a network, which is based on the idea of finding the most central nodes in the graph of the network, which are then used for the expert finding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of the results depends on the quality of the crowd.

the performance of the expert selection task is strongly dependent on the choice of the crowd: the same task may be easier to accomplish for one crowd and much harder for another, even though both crowds are drawn from the same social network.

, when the goal is to find the best possible experts, the best strategy is to choose them based on their ability to provide good recommendations, rather than their ability to provide accurate answers.
